subject: Post-discovery: coordinate ML/Infra workshop and calendar options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Patel <claire.patel@novacorp.com>, Samir Iqbal <samir.iqbal@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next step: ML/Infra workshop (60-90m)

Thanks for the time today, Claire and Samir — really helpful to understand NovaCorp's latency targets and the ingestion profile for your tagging pipeline. Short recap:
- Primary objective: reduce inference tail latency for user-facing classification under 150ms P95.
- Data flow: batched events from Kafka, peak concurrency ~600 qps in US-EAST.
- Constraints: must run within your VPC, SOC2 compliance required, and avoid token retention beyond 30 days.

Based on that, the right next step is a focused ML/Infra workshop where our infra engineers and your platform folks can walk through: environment/network requirements, model selection/quantization options, and an initial benchmarking plan. I propose 60-90 minutes so we can do a short demo, live Q&A, and calendar sync for follow-ups.

Proposed time slots (all PT):
- Tue 26 May, 10:00–11:30
- Wed 27 May, 14:00–15:30
- Thu 28 May, 09:00–10:30

Draft agenda attached (proposed-agenda.md) and a short one-pager on our serving approach (redwood-tdx-one-pager.pdf). Please let me know which slot works or share two alternatives and I'll coordinate invites.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
—
Attachments:
- redwood-tdx-one-pager.pdf (1.1MB)
- proposed-agenda.md (1.2KB)

From: Claire Patel <claire.patel@novacorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Iqbal <samir.iqbal@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step: ML/Infra workshop (60-90m)

Thanks Jordan — apreciate the clear recap. Wed 27 May 14:00 PT looks promising for us. Two quick things before we lock in: 1) we'd like to include our infra lead (Aisha Rahman) to validate VPC/network items, 2) can you confirm if there's any prep or data we should send ahead (sample request volumes, schema)?

Also, curious whether the workshop will include a short live run of one of our candidate models or if that comes in a separate session.

Claire
VP Product, NovaCorp

Great — locking Wed 27 May, 14:00–15:30 PT tentatively. Aisha, looping you in to confirm your availability for network/VPC items (we usually cover peering, private IPs, and egress rules).

Short answers to Claire's questions:
- Prep: a short sample of expected request rate distribution (5–10 lines) and the model input schema will help; no sensitive PII required.
- Live run: we can do a short live inference run if you can share a small sanitized sample. If you prefer, we can demo with a synthetic sample modeled on your schema.

Draft agenda (attached) — highlights:
1) Introductions & goals (10m)
2) Network & security constraints (20m)
3) Model / quantization tradeoffs and perf expectations (20m)
4) Live demo / micro-benchmark (20–30m)
5) Next steps & action items (10m)

If Wed 27 is confirmed, I will send the calendar invite and include a short Prep doc link.

Thanks,
Jordan

Attachments:
- proposed-agenda.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick recap + next step: ML/Infra workshop (60-90m)

Adding a few notes from the infra side — happy to lead the network/security and perf sections.
- Need clarity on NovaCorp's VPC CIDR ranges and whether there is existing peering or a transit gateway.
- For live benchmarking: prefer a sanitized batch of 100 requests that reflect the 95th percentile payload size; smaller samples are fine for an initial smoke run.
- Will bring a short checklist for required IAM roles and flamegraphs we may collect during the demo.

I'll prepare a short slide (5–6 slides) that shows quantization options (int8 vs 4-bit) and expected P95 improvements under typical batching.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
